alerts.reason: Douglas Dynamics’ net sales fell 4.58% year over year in September and 3.30% in December. The annual totals in A and the quarterly figures imply first-half 2021 sales of about $261 million, up 39%. The 2020 shutdown began March 18 and disrupted second-quarter shipments (B, C), and dealers released pent-up demand in 2021 (D). I expect March to stay above −5% and the comparison with the spring 2021 rebound to push June to −5% or worse.

Tennant’s year-over-year sales growth slowed from 3.86% in September to 1.25% in December. Annual sales in A and the quarterly figures imply first-half 2021 growth of about 16%. Pricing supported sales (D), but component shortages persisted into 2022 while backlog reached three to five times its usual size (B, C). I expect March growth to remain above −5% and delayed shipments against the stronger prior-year base to push June to −5% or worse.

Cerence’s quarterly revenue fell from $98.1 million in September to $94.4 million in December while the corresponding prior-year figure rose from $91.2 million to $93.6 million. Year-over-year growth narrowed from 7.49% to 0.84% (A). I expect its multiyear customer contracts (B) to cushion the slowdown enough to keep March above −5%, with further erosion taking June to −5% or worse.
